references.text: Bet-Hogla is also mentioned as a boundary marker for the tribe of Judah, where the border goes up to Bet-Hogla.
The Salt Sea (Dead Sea) and the Jordan River are mentioned as boundary markers, just as in Joshua 18:19.
Bet-Hogla is mentioned as one of the cities belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, which is the tribe whose borders are described in 18:19.
The Salt Sea is used as a boundary marker for the land of Israel, in the same way as in Joshua 18:19.
The Jordan River and the Salt Sea are mentioned as boundaries of the land, parallel to the border description in Joshua 18:19.
